# Event nodes: what the behaviour graph covers, and how the rest is closed

This is the design for taking the behaviour graph from 39 simulated event nodes to all 57. The table in
"Coverage" is generated by `tools/behaviour_coverage.py` from the X3D Unified Object Model and the code; a test pins
it, so the numbers here cannot drift from the code.

## What "the 57" are

An **event node** is a concrete X3D 4.0 node whose job is to make or shape events: it inherits one of
`X3DSensorNode`, `X3DInterpolatorNode`, `X3DFollowerNode`, `X3DSequencerNode`, `X3DTriggerNode`, `X3DScriptNode`,
`X3DTimeDependentNode`, or sits in the EventUtilities component, plus `EaseInEaseOut` (an interpolator in all but its
base type). The object model (X3DUOM 4.0) gives 73 such nodes. Two families are left out on purpose and listed as out
of scope, not as gaps: the 12 Web Audio processing nodes of the Sound component (signal graphs, not event logic;
`AudioClip` stays in) and the 4 DIS network nodes. 73 - 12 - 4 = **57**.

| component | nodes | count |
|---|---|---:|
| Time | TimeSensor | 1 |
| Interpolation | Color, Coordinate, Coordinate2D, Normal, Orientation, Position, Position2D, Scalar, SplinePosition, SplinePosition2D, SplineScalar, SquadOrientation interpolators, EaseInEaseOut | 13 |
| EventUtilities | BooleanFilter, BooleanSequencer, BooleanToggle, BooleanTrigger, IntegerSequencer, IntegerTrigger, TimeTrigger | 7 |
| Followers | Color, Coordinate, Orientation, Position, Position2D, Scalar, TexCoord2D: Chaser and Damper each | 14 |
| PointingDeviceSensor | TouchSensor, PlaneSensor, CylinderSensor, SphereSensor | 4 |
| KeyDeviceSensor | KeySensor, StringSensor | 2 |
| EnvironmentalSensor | ProximitySensor, VisibilitySensor, TransformSensor | 3 |
| Networking | LoadSensor | 1 |
| Geospatial | GeoPositionInterpolator, GeoProximitySensor, GeoTouchSensor | 3 |
| Picking | LinePickSensor, PointPickSensor, PrimitivePickSensor, VolumePickSensor | 4 |
| RigidBodyPhysics | CollisionSensor | 1 |
| Navigation | Collision (its `collideTime`) | 1 |
| Scripting | Script | 1 |
| Sound | AudioClip | 1 |
| Texturing | MovieTexture | 1 |

The three NURBS interpolators (`NurbsPositionInterpolator`, `NurbsOrientationInterpolator`,
`NurbsSurfaceInterpolator`) are `X3DChildNode`s in the object model and so fall outside this count; they are a
stretch package after the 57.

## Four rungs, one ladder

Coverage is not one number. Each node stands on a rung, and the table says which:

1. **Wired**: in the catalogue with typed fields, so a ROUTE to or from it is kept, shown in the node editor, and
   written back. Nothing is lost on import and export.
2. **Simulated**: `behaviour_sim` has a machine for it; events in give events out, deterministically.
3. **Judged**: a probe world was recorded on X_ITE 16.8.1 and the simulator agrees on every stream
   (`tools/behaviour_sim_judge`). A node is listed in `SIMULATED` only when it stands here. Where X_ITE does not
   implement a node or a field, the row says so and names the second referee used, or says "no referee".
4. **Played**: Blender's Player applies the result to something a person can see, or lists by name what it does not
   apply.

State on main before this work: 45 wired, 39 simulated, 38 judged (VisibilitySensor is simulated but unjudged).

## Why 18 nodes were missing: they need something the simulator did not have

The 39 are pure functions of events and time. The 18 are not. They fall into five classes by what they need, and
each class gets one small, explicit interface instead of eighteen special cases.

| class | nodes | what they need | the interface |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Lists of values | CoordinateChaser, CoordinateDamper, TexCoordChaser2D, TexCoordDamper2D | nothing new: the scalar follower run element by element | the existing follower machine, lifted over a list (as `_VectorListInterpolator` did for interpolators) |
| B. The world's shape | TransformSensor, VisibilitySensor (to be judged), Collision, GeoProximitySensor, GeoTouchSensor, the four pick sensors | where things are: boxes, spheres, points and lines in world space, and the viewer | `World`: a read-only description handed to `Simulation` (see below) |
| C. Another coordinate system | GeoPositionInterpolator, GeoProximitySensor, GeoTouchSensor | geodetic, UTM and geocentric conversion | `behaviour_geo`: pure functions, tested against X_ITE's own output |
| D. Outside resources and their clocks | LoadSensor, AudioClip, MovieTexture | whether and when a URL loads, and how long a medium lasts | `Resources`: a declared table (url -> loads after t seconds or fails; duration), part of the stimulus |
| E. Code and engines the graph cannot run | Script, CollisionSensor | a JavaScript engine; a physics engine | `Hosted`: typed ports from the node's own declarations; outputs come from a named handler or from the stimulus; with neither, the node is wired and says "hosted, not run" |

### `World` (class B)

A plain data object, no bpy: named volumes (`box`, `sphere`, `points`, `segments`) with a world matrix that the
simulation updates when a ROUTE moves a Transform it knows about, plus the viewer's position, orientation and view
frustum. Built two ways: from the X3D file (for the simulator and the judge) and from the Blender scene (for the
Player; the Player already does this for ProximitySensor, which becomes the first client of `World`). Sensors query
it once per step. Rules:

- Exactness is stated per sensor: TransformSensor and ProximitySensor test boxes exactly; pick sensors implement
  `intersectionType "BOUNDS"` exactly and `"GEOMETRY"` for Box, Sphere, PointSet and IndexedLineSet only; anything
  else is delivered as BOUNDS and counted in `Simulation.noted["bounds-for-geometry"]`.
- No silent fallbacks: a sensor whose target has no volume in `World` sends nothing and is named in
  `Simulation.noted`.
- Cost: one pass over the sensor's own targets per step; no all-pairs search. Budget below.

### `Resources` (class D)

X3D leaves loading to the browser, so a simulator must be told. `Resources` maps a URL to `{"loads": seconds}` or
`{"fails": seconds}` and, for media, `{"duration": seconds}`. It is part of the stimulus and of a recording
(`x3d.activity/1` gains an optional `resources` block), so a run is reproducible. With no entry, a URL "loads at once
with unknown duration" (-1, as the standard says for an unknown duration) and is counted in
`Simulation.noted["assumed-loaded"]`. The judge serves small local files (a WAV and a PNG made by the test itself, no
third-party asset) so X_ITE's real loading can be compared.

### `Hosted` (class E)

- **Script**: fields declared with `<field>` become typed ports (the mechanism ComposedShader uses). The simulator
  delivers events to it and records them. Outputs come from a Python handler registered by name
  (`Simulation.host("ScriptDEF", fn)`), or from the recording. The add-on never runs JavaScript. The judge can still
  watch a Script's outputs in X_ITE, so a handler can be checked against the real script.
- **CollisionSensor**: `isActive` and `contacts` come from the stimulus (`{"call": "contact", ...}`) or, in the
  Player, from Blender's own rigid body world when one exists; otherwise "hosted, not run". The simulator does not
  contain a physics engine and does not pretend to.

A hosted node counts as wired and, with a handler or stimulus, simulated. It is never counted as judged unless a
probe with a handler agrees with X_ITE.

## Rules that hold for every new node

1. X_ITE decides. Where the standard's text and X_ITE 16.8.1 differ, the simulator follows X_ITE and the difference
   is written down (as with the wrong-length `keyValue`).
2. A node enters `SIMULATED` only after its probe agrees on every stream. Existing traces are never re-recorded.
3. Hostile input never raises: bad counts, NaN, empty lists and missing targets are dropped and counted.
4. Fuzz stays at 0 failed on seeds 1 to 3, normal and hostile, and in Blender; new nodes join the fuzzer's tables.
5. Speed: `tools/behaviour_bench.py` gets one case per class (1,000 list followers of 100 points; 200 world sensors
   over 1,000 volumes; 1,000 media clocks). Budget: a step stays under 16.7 ms at those sizes on the reference
   machine, or the number is reported as a known limit. `PYTHONHASHSEED=3`.
6. What Play does not apply is listed by name.
7. Every number in the docs names the instrument that produced it.

## Work packages

Each is one spec, one agent, one worktree, one or two commits, joined by cherry-pick and re-measured together.

| # | package | nodes | depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | Coverage tool and pinned table; catalogue grows to all 57 (wired); `Hosted` ports for Script | all 57 wired | - |
| P1 | List followers | 4 | P0 |
| P2 | `World`; TransformSensor; VisibilitySensor judged; Collision.collideTime | 3 | P0 |
| P3 | `behaviour_geo`; GeoPositionInterpolator, GeoProximitySensor, GeoTouchSensor | 3 | P2 |
| P4 | Pick sensors on `World` | 4 | P2 |
| P5 | `Resources`; LoadSensor, AudioClip, MovieTexture | 3 | P0 |
| P6 | Hosted handlers for Script; CollisionSensor from stimulus and from Blender's rigid body world | 2 | P0 |
